bug_report: The average calculation crashes when the input list is empty. I expected calculate_average([]) to return 0.0.

diagnosis.summary: calculate_average divides sum(numbers) by len(numbers) with no check for an empty list.
diagnosis.root_cause: For an empty list len(numbers) is 0, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Handle the empty list before dividing.

evidence.observation: return sum(numbers) / len(numbers) has no empty-input check.

bug_report: When I call GET /users/999 for a user that does not exist, the API returns a 500 error. I expected a 404 response.

diagnosis.summary: get_user_profile reads user.id on the None that UserService.get_user returns for a missing user.
diagnosis.root_cause: UserRepository.find_by_id returns None for a missing user; get_user_profile dereferences it, and the broad except turns the AttributeError into a 500.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Return a 404 response when no user is found.

evidence.observation: user.id is read without a None check inside a broad try/except.
find_by_id returns None when no record exists.

bug_report: The last page of results is missing. With 5 items and 2 per page, page 3 should show the 5th item, but it is empty.

diagnosis.summary: total_pages uses floor division, so a partial last page is not counted.
diagnosis.root_cause: total_pages returns item_count // per_page, which rounds down; paginate then treats the partial last page as beyond the end.

bug_report: Discounts are not applied: a 10% discount on a 100.00 item still charges 100.00, and order totals ignore the discount.

diagnosis.summary: apply_discount computes the discounted price but returns the original price.
diagnosis.root_cause: apply_discount assigns the discounted value to a local variable and then returns round(price, 2) instead.

evidence.observation: discounted is computed and never used; the original price is returned.

bug_report: Starting the service with PORT=abc silently listens on 8080. An invalid PORT should fail with a ConfigError so the misconfiguration is visible.

diagnosis.summary: load_port catches every exception and returns the default port.
diagnosis.root_cause: A broad except Exception swallows the ValueError from int() and the ConfigError for out-of-range ports; only a missing PORT (KeyError) should fall back to the default.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Catch only KeyError for the default and raise ConfigError for invalid values.

evidence.observation: except Exception: return DEFAULT_PORT hides every error.

bug_report: Orders from California are charged differently depending on whether the region is typed 'CA' or 'ca': 'CA' gets no sales tax and 'ca' gets the $10 default shipping instead of $5.

diagnosis.summary: tax_rate and shipping_cost look regions up with the code exactly as given, but their tables use different cases.
diagnosis.root_cause: TAX_RATES has lower-case keys and SHIPPING upper-case keys, and both lookups are case-sensitive, so each lookup misses for one spelling of the region.

bug_report: A cache TTL of '90s' keeps entries for 90 minutes instead of 90 seconds.

diagnosis.summary: The shared duration parser maps the 's' unit to 60 seconds.
diagnosis.root_cause: UNITS in durations.py maps 's' to 60 instead of 1, so every seconds value, in the cache and in request timeouts, is read as minutes.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Map 's' to 1 in the unit table.

bug_report: Summarising an empty score list crashes with 'not enough values to unpack'. An empty input should give count 0, mean 0.0 and no best player.

diagnosis.summary: parse_scores splits blank input into one empty item, and summarize does not handle zero scores.
diagnosis.root_cause: parse_scores treats the empty string from ''.split(',') as an item and fails to unpack it; summarize then divides by zero and calls max() on an empty dict when there are no scores.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Skip blank items while parsing and return the empty summary when there are no scores.

evidence.observation: Each split item is unpacked without a blank check.
Divides by len(values) and calls max() with no empty check.

bug_report: February 2000 shows 28 days, but 2000 was a leap year.

diagnosis.summary: is_leap_year implements the 4-year and century rules but not the 400-year rule.
diagnosis.root_cause: is_leap_year returns year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0, so years divisible by 400, such as 2000, are wrongly not leap years.

bug_report: Slugs drop accented letters: 'Café au lait' becomes 'caf-au-lait' instead of 'cafe-au-lait'.

diagnosis.summary: slugify keeps only [a-z0-9] after lower-casing, so non-ASCII letters are discarded.
diagnosis.root_cause: slugify matches [a-z0-9]+ on the raw lower-cased title, which drops accented letters instead of transliterating them to ASCII.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Transliterate to ASCII before matching words.

bug_report: Splitting a $100.00 bill between 3 people charges $33.33 each, so the shares add up to $99.99 and a cent goes missing.

diagnosis.summary: split_bill rounds one share and repeats it, so leftover cents are lost.
diagnosis.root_cause: split_bill computes round(total_cents / people) once and returns that share for everyone, so whenever the total does not divide evenly the shares do not add up to the total.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Distribute the leftover cents so the shares add up to the total.

evidence.observation: One rounded share is repeated for every person.

bug_report: The updater says version 1.10.0 is not newer than 1.9.0, so users on 1.9.0 are never offered the update.

diagnosis.root_cause: is_newer returns candidate > current on the raw strings, so '1.10.0' sorts before '1.9.0' because '1' < '9' character by character.

bug_report: The contact list shows Ada@x.com and ada@X.com as two different people. Addresses that differ only in case should appear once.

diagnosis.root_cause: unique_emails uses dict.fromkeys(emails), which compares addresses case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are kept as separate entries.
